summary.headline: TII Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% to Rs 2,366 Cr, but PBT fell to Rs 213 Cr on steel cost lag; management expects full recovery.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew to Rs 2,366 Cr from Rs 2,007 Cr, while standalone PBT declined to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 222 Cr, with management attributing margin pressure to steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 that pass through to customers with a 2-3 quarter lag. Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,566 Cr vs Rs 1,298 Cr YoY; PBIT flat at Rs 153 Cr. Volume grew about 17%, and margins were hit by steel cost inflation.

segments.name: Metal Formed Products (MFP)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 408 Cr vs Rs 366 Cr YoY (about 11.5%), but PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr. Growth was volume-led, with railways a drag and a Hyundai-linked unit weak; a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

segments.name: Mobility (Clean Mobility / e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 250 Cr vs Rs 198 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 9 Cr vs Rs 7 Cr. Management cited highest-ever turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr (the call figure), with negative EBIT narrowing by about Rs 40-50 Cr per analyst, and three-wheeler billing of 1,924 units.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 256 Cr vs Rs 236 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 21 Cr vs Rs 17 Cr. Includes TI Medical, CDMO (3xper) and Orange Koi, the newly acquired metal injection moulding start-up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects steel price increases, including the Q1 under-recovery, to be fully recovered with a lag, with margin neutralisation in coming quarters.
Management declined to quantify the Q1 under-recovery but reiterated guidance for double-digit EBIT margin growth.
Non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery under discussion with OEMs; update expected in about one quarter.
Cycles business: management targets about 2 bps (as stated, likely 2 percentage points) further margin improvement for FY27 to reach about 5% margin.
TI Medical core surgical business expected to grow about 20% YoY with profitability; IV cannula acquisition plant to start revenue from August/September 2026.
Jayem expected to add a battery business stream; one EV business expected to break even in FY27, and two more in FY28.
Rs 750 Cr total capital infusion into new ventures over time; Rs 250 Cr infused in Q4 FY26, another Rs 250 Cr expected in Q3 FY27.
Management expects engineering demand to remain bullish for the next one or two quarters, barring geopolitical disruption.
capex_capacity: TI standalone capex planned at about Rs 350 Cr for FY27; Shanthi Gears about Rs 100 Cr; group ex-CG Power about Rs 600-700 Cr, per CFO.
Capex directed to engineering and MFP divisions, plus TI Medical and 3xper CDMO.
3xper CDMO 200 KL intermediate capacity: commissioning done, validation batches underway, clean room commissioning in 30-40 days, customer PAS filing and inspection expected in FY28.
Greenfield MFP plant in western region delayed by six months.
Clean Mobility: L3 autos introduced in select UP and Bihar markets on a test basis; tipper (28-ton) sold about 20-25 units, with market shifting to 35-ton and above.
demand_pricing: Engineering volume grew about 17% in Q1; management said exports grew strongly with double-digit growth; exports are about 14% of TI revenue.
Steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 caused margin compression; pass-through lag of 2-3 quarters.
Cycles business benefited from strong Q1 seasonality (schools and colleges reopening) with higher market share.
Clean Mobility billing volumes in Q1: 86 heavy trucks, 1,924 three-wheelers, 347 small commercial vehicles, 22 tractors. Three-wheeler FY26 billing about 6,700 vs Vahan registrations about 6,500.
Cell prices expected to stay firm through at least Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders.
Nepal: about 100+ three-wheeler units shipped or in process; African markets (Tanzania, Ethiopia) at exploratory stage.
HCV deployments: about 22 trucks at Welspun's Anjar port, plus single-digit deployments at Vizag and Chennai ports, and Wonder Cement at Tuna and Dahej ports.
